# PR #297: PASS WITH NOTES, final round under C34

Head: `519843289b4c8eeb068cb9d96ab9e16f392b26d3`.
Request: `01a1f9f1-18bf-7ef2-9783-79a299ae7c7a`.

**R297-001 is closed.** Reviewed the repair commits `e928ead0`, `56a9dfd0`
and `51984328`, including the complete shared-build script and test file.
The intervening merge of main's #295 is not a new review scope.

## Fix verification

The same real-cargo A -> B(build, then failed check) -> A reproduction that
returned B in round 1 now recompiles A and returns **A**, with
`--target aarch64-apple-darwin`. B's failed batch leaves `running B`;
returning A leaves `finished A`. A subsequent build reports 0.00 s, compiles
nothing, leaves source mtimes unchanged and still returns A.

The same runner verifies adoption: after B builds, a future-dated bare A stamp
is planted to reproduce the trusted legacy state. Corrected A touches,
recompiles and returns A; its next run is fresh. Thus the repair does not
silently retain a poisoned round-1 stamp.

An independent fake-cargo state oracle verifies that:

- Cargo observes `running <its tree>` before it executes.
- A waiting B cannot enter or replace A's running stamp while A holds the lock.
  SIGTERM drains A before B enters, and successful B publishes `finished B`.
- A batch failing after its first successful command leaves `running B` even
  when it wrote no deps artifact; returning A touches and publishes `finished A`.

The lock still encloses invalidation, running publication, every cargo command,
finished publication and copy-out. Cargo failure exits before `finished`;
copy-out failure may retain `finished` because the cargo artifacts are complete.
A target absent before the first cargo command has no trusted stamp to preserve.
The all-depth find detects explicit-target deps; its bookkeeping pruning does
not exclude the reproduced target-triple layout.

The committed 26-case suite now covers the missing layout, failed batches,
legacy adoption and newer bare-cargo triple/release artifacts. Its stamp-path
test also covers the reported symlink-to-directory behavior. Security owns the
separate C33 check/rename residual.

## Accepted residual: F246

The prime's C34 ruling, relayed by pm-001 in message
`b764488df75ee6cf-0000000000000038`, says this ships named **F246**, folded into
the coder's F245 PR: stamp-publication failure can leave an earlier finished
stamp trusted; the follow-up must invalidate and warn. This is disclosed in
the PR's Residual section. No publication-failure runtime proof is claimed.
The existing F226 release-build version/HEAD check remains an additional
deployment guard, not a reason to erase the residual.

This is PASS WITH NOTES, not a third-round block or a claim that F246 is fixed.

## Evidence

- `nice -n 19 node pr297-r2-explicit-target-probe.mjs`: PASS, exit 0.
  Real cargo, exact-head copied scripts and just recipe, isolated target,
  niceness 19, four jobs, no dependencies downloaded. Three checks passed:
  R297-001 executable identity, same-tree reuse and poisoned-stamp adoption.
  Raw receipt: `pr297-r2-explicit-target-probe.log`.
- `nice -n 19 node pr297-r2-state-probe.mjs`: PASS, exit 0.
  Exact helper, isolated fake cargo; interruption/concurrency and no-deps
  failed-batch state checks passed. Raw receipt: `pr297-r2-state-probe.log`.
- CI run `44780085069`, attempt 1: SUCCESS at this exact full SHA.
  Node 22 job `136440126993` reports shared-build **26/26**, full TS
  **2,385 passed**, seven skipped. Receipt: `pr297-r2-ci-node22.log`.
  Rust job `136440126653` reports **2,689 passed**, six skipped.
  Its successful upload artifact `14650689845` confirms all **14**
  build-stamp/bounce cases passed. Receipts: `pr297-r2-ci-rust.log`,
  `pr297-r2-junit-summary.json`.
- `bash -n harness/scripts/shared-build.sh` and
  `git diff --check 2d983f7d HEAD`: PASS.
- `harness boot`: dependency-not-ready. `harness checks --quick --json`:
  exit 1, eight unavailable/incompatible local TS-tooling stages.
  Receipt: `pr297-r2-checks-quick.log`. No install or node_modules link under
  C25. No green local full-harness claim; exact-head CI is the TS evidence.
- F244's recipe and build-stamp tests are unchanged since round 1; their
  exact-head CI proof was checked rather than rerunning the production
  workspace. Prior round-1 macOS 14/14 and clippy remain attributed to round 1.
  No new local full-workspace build, live daemon bounce or mutation run.

## Cost and harness feedback

No new daemon loop or per-seat launches. Existing-target success uses two
absolute-path mktemp/mv pairs and zero or one absolute-path find; the scan
short-circuits unless the last stamp is this tree's finished stamp. Failure
cleanup may add rm. The coder's retained scan receipt reports 44-50 ms with
9,730 deps entries; that measurement was read, not rerun here. F244's extra
failure-path sleeps remain invocation-only.

magicWand: permanent artifact-identity/adoption proof, rather than a native-only
mtime fixture. This review's original gap is now encoded by the new regression;
the real-cargo receipt independently confirms its intended result.

difficulties: publication failure remains explicitly tracked as F246 instead of
being hidden by the pass label or expanding into a third review round.

No product edits, deployment, production signals or pushes. The reviewer/297
holding remains until merge.
